cond_0127.intro: [Company name masked] is seeking an experienced and skilled laboratory research associate to actively support the Company's promising R&D strategy for the development of novel cancer radiotherapeutic agents and related technology. The qualified individual will have 3 to 5 years prior experience in an academic or industry lab setting performing in vitro and in vivo experimental research studies. The candidate in this role is expected to support preclinical drug discovery and pharmacology studies in rodents and be proficient in oncology animal models.
cond_0127.responsibilities: Perform IACUC approved small animal experiments including in vivo mouse cancer models. Administer drugs by multiple routes including IV, IP and SC. Tumor volume and body weight measurements, tissue and blood collection. Mouse monitoring and housekeeping (e.g. Cage changing). Assist with ordering of reagents and laboratory supplies. Assist in maintaining laboratory equipment and supplies; coordinate preventative maintenance and repairs as needed. Ensure that safe laboratory practices are followed, including the use and disposal of chemicals and hazardous materials. Collect data, prepare and maintain detailed records in a laboratory notebook. Write protocols and study summary reports. Communicate study findings to team and management.
cond_0127.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor of Science degree: Biology, pharmacology or related field
3-5 Years of lab research experience
Experience handling small animals and in vivo procedures
Excellent organizational skills, detail oriented
Strong interpersonal and communication skills
Ability to work in a team setting
Preferred Requirements
Experience in the handling and use of radioactive material
Experience in mammalian cell culture

cond_0129.intro:
[Company name masked] is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing radiopharmaceutical therapeutics for the treatment of disease, particularly cancer. Our Antibody Radiation-Conjugates (ARCs) combine the tumor targeting ability of antibodies with the cell killing ability of radiation. [Company name masked] possesses proprietary expertise and know-how for the development of novel ARCs armed with the potent alpha emitting radionuclide warhead Actinium-225 (225Ac). With our technology and development capabilities, we are advancing a multi-disease, multi-target pipeline of preclinical and clinical-stage ARCs for targeted conditioning and as therapeutics for the treatment of hematologic malignancies and solid tumors. Building on our expertise and leadership in radiopharmaceuticals, [Company name masked] is rapidly accelerating our investigational research efforts and is looking for talented scientists to join the team.

Assist in maintaining laboratory equipment and supplies; coordinate preventative maintenance and repairs as needed. Ensure that safe laboratory practices are followed, including the use and disposal of chemicals and hazardous materials. Collect data, prepare and maintain detailed records in a laboratory notebook. Our Antibody Radiation-Conjugates (ARCs) combine the tumor targeting ability of antibodies with the cell killing ability of radiation. With our technology and development capabilities, we are advancing a multi-disease, multi-target pipeline of preclinical and clinical-stage ARCs for targeted conditioning and as therapeutics for the treatment of hematologic malignancies and solid tumors. Building on our expertise and leadership in radiopharmaceuticals, [Company name masked] is rapidly accelerating our investigational research efforts and is looking for talented scientists to join the team.

cond_0166.intro:

With our technology and development capabilities, we are advancing a multi-disease, multi-target pipeline of preclinical and clinical-stage ARCs for targeted conditioning and as therapeutics for the treatment of hematologic malignancies and solid tumors.
[Company name masked] is seeking an experienced and skilled laboratory research associate to actively support the Company's promising R&D strategy for the development of novel cancer radiotherapeutic agents and related technology. The qualified individual will have 3 to 5 years prior experience in an academic or industry lab setting performing in vitro and in vivo experimental research studies. The candidate in this role is expected to support preclinical drug discovery and pharmacology studies in rodents and be proficient in oncology animal models. Ensure that safe laboratory practices are followed, including the use and disposal of chemicals and hazardous materials. Collect data, prepare and maintain detailed records in a laboratory notebook. Write protocols and study summary reports. Communicate study findings to team and management.

cond_0179.intro:
[Company name masked] is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing radiopharmaceutical therapeutics for the treatment of disease, particularly cancer. Our Antibody Radiation-Conjugates (ARCs) combine the tumor targeting ability of antibodies with the cell killing ability of radiation. [Company name masked] possesses proprietary expertise and know-how for the development of novel ARCs armed with the potent alpha emitting radionuclide warhead Actinium-225 (225Ac). With our technology and development capabilities, we are advancing a multi-disease, multi-target pipeline of preclinical and clinical-stage ARCs for targeted conditioning and as therapeutics for the treatment of hematologic malignancies and solid tumors. Building on our expertise and leadership in radiopharmaceuticals, [Company name masked] is rapidly accelerating our investigational research efforts and is looking for talented scientists to join the team.
[Company name masked] is seeking an experienced laboratory research associate to own support of the Company's R&D strategy for the development of novel cancer radiotherapeutic agents and related technology. The qualified individual will have 3 to 5 years prior experience in an academic or industry lab setting performing in vitro and in vivo experimental research studies. The candidate will take ownership of preclinical drug discovery and pharmacology studies in rodents and be proficient in oncology animal models.
cond_0179.responsibilities: Execute IACUC approved small animal experiments including in vivo mouse cancer models. Administer drugs by multiple routes including IV, IP and SC. Lead tumor volume and body weight measurements, tissue and blood collection. Manage mouse monitoring and housekeeping (e.g. Cage changing). Direct ordering of reagents and laboratory supplies. Maintain laboratory equipment and supplies; coordinate preventative maintenance and repairs as needed. Ensure that safe laboratory practices are followed, including the use and disposal of chemicals and hazardous materials. Collect data, prepare and maintain detailed records in a laboratory notebook. Write protocols and study summary reports. Deliver study findings to team and management.

Bachelor of Science degree: Biology, pharmacology or related field
3-5 Years of lab research experience
Experience handling small animals and in vivo procedures is required
Experience in the handling and use of radioactive material is desirable
Experience in mammalian cell culture is desirable
Excellent organizational skills, detail oriented
Strong interpersonal and communication skills
Ability to work in a team setting

[Company name masked] is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing radiopharmaceutical therapeutics for the treatment of disease, particularly cancer. Our Antibody Radiation-Conjugates (ARCs) combine the tumor targeting ability of antibodies with the cell killing ability of radiation. [Company name masked] possesses proprietary expertise and know-how for the development of novel ARCs armed with the potent alpha emitting radionuclide warhead Actinium-225 (225Ac). With our technology and development capabilities, we are advancing a multi-disease, multi-target pipeline of preclinical and clinical-stage ARCs for targeted conditioning and as therapeutics for the treatment of hematologic malignancies and solid tumors.
[Company name masked] is seeking an experienced and skilled laboratory research associate to actively support the Company's promising R&D strategy for the development of novel cancer radiotherapeutic agents and related technology. The qualified individual will have 3 to 5 years prior experience in an academic or industry lab setting performing in vitro and in vivo experimental research studies. The candidate in this role is expected to support preclinical drug discovery and pharmacology studies in rodents and be proficient in oncology animal models. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of radiopharmaceutical research and in vivo study design.

Assist in maintaining laboratory equipment and supplies; coordinate preventative maintenance and repairs as needed. Ensure that safe laboratory practices are followed, including the use and disposal of chemicals and hazardous materials. Collect data, prepare and maintain detailed records in a laboratory notebook. Write protocols and study summary reports. Communicate study findings to team and management.

We are looking for a Laboratory Research Associate to join our team. [Company name masked] is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing radiopharmaceutical therapeutics for cancer treatment. Our Antibody Radiation-Conjugates (ARCs) combine the tumor targeting ability of antibodies with the cell killing ability of radiation. [Company name masked] possesses proprietary expertise in the development of novel ARCs armed with the alpha emitting radionuclide Actinium-225 (225Ac), and is advancing a multi-disease, multi-target pipeline of preclinical and clinical-stage ARCs for hematologic malignancies and solid tumors.
The role supports the Company's R&D strategy for the development of novel cancer radiotherapeutic agents and related technology. The qualified individual will have 3 to 5 years of prior experience in an academic or industry lab setting performing in vitro and in vivo experimental research studies. The candidate is expected to support preclinical drug discovery and pharmacology studies in rodents and be proficient in oncology animal models.
cond_0430.responsibilities:
Perform IACUC approved small animal experiments including in vivo mouse cancer models.
Administer drugs by multiple routes including IV, IP and SC.
Conduct tumor volume and body weight measurements, tissue and blood collection.
Carry out mouse monitoring and housekeeping (e.g. Cage changing).
Assist with ordering of reagents and laboratory supplies.
Assist in maintaining laboratory equipment and supplies; coordinate preventative maintenance and repairs as needed.
Ensure that safe laboratory practices are followed, including the use and disposal of chemicals and hazardous materials.
Collect data, prepare and maintain detailed records in a laboratory notebook.
Write protocols and study summary reports.
Document study findings and share with relevant team members and management.
cond_0430.requirements:
Bachelor of Science degree in Biology, pharmacology or related field
3-5 Years of lab research experience
Experience handling small animals and in vivo procedures is required
Experience in the handling and use of radioactive material is desirable
Experience in mammalian cell culture is desirable
Excellent organizational skills, detail oriented
Strong written communication and clear, direct verbal reporting
Ability to work in a team setting

[Company name masked] is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing radiopharmaceutical therapeutics for cancer treatment. Our Antibody Radiation-Conjugates (ARCs) combine the tumor targeting ability of antibodies with the cell killing ability of radiation. [Company name masked] possesses proprietary expertise in the development of novel ARCs armed with the alpha emitting radionuclide Actinium-225 (225Ac), and is advancing a multi-disease, multi-target pipeline of preclinical and clinical-stage ARCs for hematologic malignancies and solid tumors.
The role supports the Company's R&D strategy for the development of novel cancer radiotherapeutic agents and related technology. The qualified individual will have 3 to 5 years of prior experience in an academic or industry lab setting performing in vitro and in vivo experimental research studies. The candidate is expected to support preclinical drug discovery and pharmacology studies in rodents and be proficient in oncology animal models.

Ensure that safe laboratory practices are followed, including the use and disposal of chemicals and hazardous materials.
Collect data, prepare and maintain detailed records in a laboratory notebook.
Write protocols and study summary reports.
Document study findings and share with relevant team members and management.
